subject: Compliance request prioritization & runbook sync
messages:
From: Ava Johnson <ava.j@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.com>
Cc: security@lumen.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-term retention exception + evidence runbook

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. Lumen's security team ran our SOC review this week and flagged two asks that we need Redwood to support for the pilot: a temporary retention carveout for processed embeddings (30 days -> 90 days for a small subset of buckets) and a prescriptive evidence-gathering runbook for audit evidence (logs + key rotation artifacts).

They're asking for an opinion on feasibility and a proposed owner/ETA so we can include this in our SOW addendum. I've attached the compliance_request_form.pdf and their high-level retention_matrix.

Can someone from product/security confirm whether we can implement a short-lived retention policy for a dedicated dataset and what telemetry we can provide to satisfy evidence needs?

Appreciate a quick read and any suggested owners + timeline.

Best,
Ava

Attachments: compliance_request_form.pdf, retention_matrix_v2.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Ava Johnson <ava.j@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term retention exception + evidence runbook

Thanks Ava — forwarding to product/security owners. Quick read: looks scoped to a single customer namespace and a small set of embedding buckets.

Jonas / Grace — can you weigh in on the two asks below? My suggested split:
- Feasibility / runtime gating (Jonas) -> can we expose a per-namespace retention override scoped to a dedicated dataset in Redwood Dedicated / Private?
- Evidence runbook / audit artifacts (Grace) -> can Security produce a short runbook (steps + logs + locations) we can hand Lumen so they have repeatable evidence for SOC review.

If this is doable, Lumen wants an owner and ETA to put in SOW. I'm mindful we may need an exception flow for retention beyond default product promises.

Marissa
Product Lead, Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Ava Johnson <ava.j@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 08:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term retention exception + evidence runbook

Marissa — quick triage notes after a sync with infra:

- Retention override: technically feasible for Dedicated and Private where namespace isolation exists. We can implement a config flag per-namespace that adjusts retention for embeddings and associated KV artifacts. For Hosted, current infra doesn't support per-account retention overrides without infra changes and risk to caching behavior.
- Scope: recommended approach is to target a single Dedicated pool / private deployment for the pilot. That avoids product risk and keeps exposure limited.
- Work effort: estimated 2 engineering sprints (4 weeks) to add a controlled retention override, test KV expiry interactions, and add a UI/API flag. Need product approval for an exception workflow and legal signoff for SOW wording.

Action items I propose:
1) Product sign-off on pilot scope (Dedicated only) -> Marissa
2) Security to draft an evidence runbook and list of artifacts we can reliably produce -> Grace
3) Sales to confirm SOW language and whether Lumen requires Hosted support -> Ben

Jonas
Director, Serving Runtime
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Ava Johnson <ava.j@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term retention exception + evidence runbook

Marissa / Jonas — draft runbook attached (runbook-draft.md). High-level:
- Evidence bundle contents we can reliably produce: ingestion logs (time window), model-id + version hashes, KV cache eviction logs, audit log slices (admin actions), KMS key rotation events with timestamps.
- Limitations: we cannot produce tenant-level raw token streams for Hosted customers; we can provide metadata and redacted examples.
- Delivery: I can produce a human-readable runbook + a one-page evidence checklist for auditors in 5 business days if we agree on scope.

Note on keys: For customers with BYOK we can include HSM rotation timestamps from the KMS audit; for Redwood-managed keys we can provide rotation history but not HSM attestation.

Next steps: confirm which deployment mode Lumen will utilize for the pilot. If Dedicated/Private, we can proceed with the 4-week ETA for the retention override + 5-day runbook delivery.

Grace
Security Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook-draft.md
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Johnson <ava.j@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short-term retention exception & runbook sync — decision summary

Quick summary for SOW / sales:
- Agreed pilot scope: Dedicated-only pilot for Lumen Health (customer to sign Dedicated addendum).
- Engineering ETA: retention override feature will be delivered in 4 weeks (target: 2027-07-28).
- Security ETA: final evidence runbook and auditor checklist delivered by 2027-07-05.
- Legal / Procurement asks: product to provide an exception clause sample; sales to confirm whether Lumen needs a time-limited SLA change.
- Attachments shared with customer: compliance_request_form.pdf (original), runbook-draft.md (internal draft).

Ben will own SOW language and procurement coordination. Marissa to confirm with customer whether Dedicated addendum is acceptable and to update HubSpot.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Enterprises
Redwood Inference
